title: 0: Origin
description: A flashback to past podcasts, as a way of explaining why this podcast exists.
exclusion_reason: "0: Origin" is a compilation of rulings that were re-ruled in their own later episodes; a majority of its subjects repeat elsewhere in the scorecard.

title: 1: Mr. Roboto
description: We explain why we’re here, and then discuss the protagonist of Styx’s 1983 album “Kilroy Was Here.”

title: 2: Service Kiosks
description: John’s position on supermarket self-checkout machines, Jason’s need for beer when he visits his in-laws, and whether attaching arms to things makes them robots.

title: 3: Darth Vader
description: Cyborgs and robots and humans—how do we tell these things apart?

title: 4: K-9
description: John and Jason try to understand robot dogs. Plus, a trip through old “Doctor Who” episodes.

title: 5: Emotions
description: The greatest prog rock album ever made.

title: 6: Self-Driving Cars
description: Pondering sentient Google cars, Johnny Cab, and autopilots.

title: 7: Telepresence Robots
description: They’re funny, but are they robots?

title: 8: Roomba
description: Does a self-guided vacuum cleaner cross John’s minimum bar for a robot? And what does that have to do with ants and dogs?

title: 9: Assembly-Line Robots
description: Look for the union label.

title: 10: ASIMO
description: Honda’s ASIMO, Sony’s AIBO, and other cute things that can do The Robot dance. Also, our Radio Shack memories.

title: 11: KITT
description: The “Knight Rider” car is cool, but is it a robot? What about KITT’s evil twin, KARR? Also, the dark pre-history of Pixar’s “Cars.”

title: 12: USS Enterprise
description: The main computer of the USS Enterprise.

title: 13: Transformers
description: Like the song says.

title: 14: Jaegers
description: Big robots with people inside, as seen in “Shogun Warriors” and “Pacific Rim.”

title: 15: The Major
description: From “Ghost in the Shell,” a human brain in a mechanical body. And what about uploaded brains and bodies?

title: 16: Siri
description: So-called intelligent agents.

title: 17: The Terminator
description: I know now why you humans cry.

title: 18: Commander Data
description: Is an android a robot?

title: 19: Marvin the Paranoid Android
description: Your plastic pal who’s fun to be with!

title: 20: Pinocchio
description: Are we seriously talking about magic here?

title: 21: Droids
description: Are droids robots? Do they have rights? Is the Empire based on a robo-slave economy?

title: 22: Hitchbot
description: He tried to hitch his way across the country, but was dismembered in Philadelphia. Image by archier on Flickr.

title: 23: Space Probes
description: From golf carts on Mars to New Horizons flying past Pluto, these are impressive machines, but are they robots?

title: 24: Sasquatch
description: The bigfoot/sasquatch from “The Six Million Dollar Man.”

title: 25: Home Appliances
description: What would a toaster have to do in order to be a robot? This episode introduces Siracusa’s Law, which somehow involves kitchen countertops.

title: 26: Cylons
description: The metal robots (and their fleshy successors) from the old and new “Battlestar Galactica.”

title: 27: V'ger
description: V’ger and the Ilia probe, both from “Star Trek: The Motion Picture”. Also, John complains about fake skin on androids.

title: 28: The TARDIS
description: The blue box from “Doctor Who” might be sentient, might be alive, but is it a robot?

title: 29: Johnny 5
description: That little guy from “Short Circuit.”

title: 30: Twiki and Dr. Theopolis
description: We take you back to the days of “Buck Rogers in the 25th Century” to debate the show’s two artificial sidekicks.

title: 31: robots.txt
description: It’s right there in the name, but what about the things that connect to it? And what about when Merlin talks about putting things “in the robot”? We need answers, John!

title: 32: Lobot
description: Cloud City’s majordomo from “The Empire Strikes Back” is in the spotlight.

title: 33: Vicki from "Small Wonder"
description: She’s a small wonder, pretty and bright with soft curls. She’s a small wonder, a girl unlike other girls. She’s a miracle, and I grant you She’ll enchant you at her sight. She’s a small wonder, and she’ll make your heart take flight. She’s fantastic, made of plastic. Microchips here and there. She’s a small wonder, brings love and laughter everywhere.

title: 34: Aperture Science
description: GlaDOS, Wheatley, turrets, cubes, spheres and more.

title: 35: Herbie The Love Bug
description: A Volkswagen Beetle with a mind of his own!

title: 36: Iron Man, Ultron, and Vision
description: From the Marvel Cinematic Universe, and specifically “Iron Man 3” and “Avengers: Age of Ultron,” deep robot-or-not questions about Iron Man’s suits, Ultron, and the Vision.

title: 37: Clockwork Droids
description: Doctor Who’s clockwork repair droids (from the episodes “Girl in the Fireplace” and “Deep Breath”) come under scrutiny. Sure, they start out as robots, but do they become something else..?

title: 38: Podcasts
description: Just in time for the holidays, some existential questions. Also, could a robot be on a podcast?

title: 39: Cars (from "Cars")
description: If the cars in Pixar’s “Cars” movies aren’t cars, what are they, and where did they come from?

title: 40: Swimming Pool Cleaners
description: Things that clean your swimming pool: are they Roombas or just dumb hoses? Also, if a toaster can’t be a robot, can a robot be a toaster?

title: 41: Burritos
description: This one seems to have gotten in by mistake.

title: 42: Prince Robot IV
description: It’s right there in the name of this character from the acclaimed comic book “Saga,” but as we’ve learned, names can be misleading.

title: 43: Daleks and Cybermen
description: Two enemies wrapped in metal shells from “Doctor Who” face their ultimate foe—the judgment of John Siracusa.

title: 44: The Internet of Things
description: Security expert Bruce Schneier said the Internet of Things was a robot, but what does John think? You can probably guess.

title: 45: Nanobots
description: Enter the realm of the very, very tiny as John and Jason ponder if size matters when it comes to whether something is a robot or not.

title: 46: Crow T. Robot and Tom Servo
description: The bots from “Mystery Science Theater 3000.”

title: 47: Thomas and Friends
description: Living rail cars in Sodor.

title: 48: Replicants
description: Roy Batty, Pris, and all the rest. They’ve seen the Tannhauser Gate, but are they robots?

title: 49: Chatbots
description: They listen to us and talk back. But is that enough?

title: 50: The Matrix
description: Agents and Oracles and Architects from the “Matrix” trilogy.

title: 51: Lego Simulated Worm Toy
description: A software model of a flatworm, piloting a Lego Mindstorms toy.

title: 52: The Robots of "Destiny"
description: From Bungie’s bestselling video game, Ghosts, Exos, Rasputin, and other things that might be robots.

title: 53: Tamagotchi
description: Is it even a game? What if you had a video game that featured a robot?

title: 54: T-1000
description: It’s made of liquid metal.

title: 55: The Tin Woodman
description: If he only had a heart.

title: 56: The Incomparable's Logo
description: Our own robot (or not) is in the spotlight at last.

title: 57: Baymax
description: He’s an inflatable, medical robot from “Big Hero 6”—but can you back up your personality and still be a robot?

title: 58: Synths
description: From the AMC TV series “Humans,” the lifelike Synths look like humans but don’t act like it. And they bleed a funny color.

title: 59: The Doctor from "Star Trek: Voyager"
description: Please state the nature of the medical emergency. Can a hologram be a robot?

title: 60: Inspector Gadget
description: Go go Gadget! Also we get off on a tangent about Penny, inspired by The Flop House.

title: 61: Elevators
description: They go up, they go down. They might even go sideways from time to time. And they can be smart. But are they robots?

title: 62: General Grievous
description: He’s a droid with a cough. So what’s the deal?

title: 63: Animatronic Creatures
description: The Country Bears, Chuck E. Cheese, and the things from Five Nights at Freddy’s.

title: 64: Rossum's Universal Robots
description: Karel Capek’s play that made this podcast possible.

title: 65: Serena Williams
description: It’s Wimbledon time, and so our discussion turns to tennis, and Serena Williams—who is not a robot, despite her perhaps wishing she was.

title: 66: Traffic lights in South Africa
description: Please obey robot.

title: 67: Silicone Stingray
description: Part animal, part machine. But is it a robot?

title: 68: Canadarm
description: A fancy “robot arm” from Canada. But when is a robot arm just an arm, and when is it a robot?

title: 69: Tron
description: He fights for the users inside a computer. Can software people be robots?

title: 70: The Robots of "Futurama"
description: Bender, Calculon, and Hedonismbot.

title: 71: RoboCop
description: That “Robo” prefix is sure interesting, and he’s probably a cop, but…

title: 72: Robots from "Castle in the Sky" and "The Iron Giant"
description: Two beloved metal creatures from animation.

title: 73: Cartoons
description: Is all animation “cartoons”?

title: 74: Gort
description: The robot from “The Day the Earth Stood Still”, plus a long digression into Star Trek androids.

title: 75: Bubo
description: A little metal owl from “Clash of the Titans.” Crafted by the gods, can he possibly be a robot?

title: 76: Animals in "Blade Runner"
description: The owl and the snake from “Blade Runner” raise some interesting questions.

title: 77: Daft Punk
description: They sure look like robots. But who’s under the masks?

title: 78: Hot Dogs
description: They’re sure tasty, and it’s meat between bread, but are hot dogs sandwiches?

title: 79: SpaceX
description: Self-guided rockets and drone barges.

title: 80: Tachikoma and Fuchikoma
description: Little cute robots from “Ghost in the Shell.”

title: 81: The Energizer Bunny
description: It just keeps going, and going, and going….

title: 82: The Borg
description: Straight out of “Star Trek” come these technological villains. Also, we discuss larger issues including AIs and hive minds.

title: 83: Kayaks
description: They are boats with paddles. What else are they?

title: 84: Metal Mario
description: Sometimes Mario is metallic. Does that make him a robot?

title: 85: The Bicentennial Man
description: A robot slowly turns himself human. When does he stop being a robot?

title: 86: The Hosts of "Westworld"
description: The HBO series “Westworld” makes us contemplate whether its central characters, the Hosts, are robots or not. (We recorded this episode after the first seven episodes of season one had aired; forgive us if it was revealed later that “To Serve Man” was actually a cookbook.)

title: 87: K5 Mall Robot
description: It patrols the mall. Sometimes it knocks over small children.

title: 88: School Babies and CPR Dummies
description: High school students carry them around and learn what it’s like to be a parent. Or you learn how to revive them by pressing their chest and breathing into their mouths. But are these learning tools also educational robots?

title: 89: Battlebots
description: Among the fiercest creatures in the machine kingdom are the Battlebots. They’re designed for fighting! But are they really robots, or is that just a clever marketing name?

title: 90: Mechagodzilla
description: Look who was under the tree! It’s a giant mechanical monster!

title: 91: Naked Robotic Core
description: An unadorned iPhone can be a Naked Robotic Core, but is it a robot?

title: 92: Pronunciation
description: ˈrōˌbät or ˈrōbət?

title: 93: Nintendo R.O.B.
description: Game controller, robot, or total embarrassment?

title: 94: Shardik
description: The robotic guardian of the Beams. He looks like a bear but has a satellite dish on his head. He’s a thousand years old.

title: 95: Autonomous Sailboats
description: They roam the ocean, scanning for important data and relaying their information home. There are no humans on board. Are these lonely sea voyagers robots?

title: 96: The Gate at Jabba's Palace
description: The gate at Jabba’s palace in “Return of the Jedi” talks to droids, or has something inside it that talks to droids. So is it a robot?

title: 97: Captchas
description: What does a robot do when it gets to a web page with a checkbox that says “I’m not a robot”?

title: 98: Human Beings
description: Could it be? Are we all robots?

title: 99: Your Hosts
description: Are John and Jason robots? All will be revealed!

title: 100: The Robot
description: Your hosts return to where it all began and then prepare to set out for new horizons. (Robot or Not will return in two weeks with a new series of episodes.)

title: 101: Supervillains
description: John helps Jason figure out the precise moment when a villain becomes a supervillain.

title: 102: Sandwiches
description: Exploring what makes a sandwich, while also discussing the history of food, sandwiches as satire, and the difference between llamas and camels.

title: 103: Pizza
description: John weighs in on what makes something a pizza, including the horror of the Turkey Dinner Pizza.

title: 104: Pizza Toppings
description: What toppings are allowed on pizza? And what about using a knife and fork to eat pizza? There are many rules.

title: 105: Canonical Bagel Flavors
description: What is the canon of bagels? Why are some ingredients allowed in an Everything Bagel but not any other bagel style? What makes raisins an acceptable ingredient, yet bars blueberries? Mr. Siracusa, native of the great state of New York, educates Mr. Snell, one of those California hippie types, about what a real bagel is.

title: 106: Computer Chips
description: Is everything a computer chip? Is nothing a computer chip? Jason thinks this is gonna be good. John thinks it’s obvious.

title: 107: Science Fiction
description: What’s science fiction? And more importantly, is Star Wars science fiction, fantasy, or something else?

title: 108: Condiments and Favorite Foods
description: Exploring Jason’s favorite food, what a “favorite food” even is, and the hazy dividing line between condiments and other edibles.

title: 109: Sport
description: What makes something a sport, and not an exercise or a game?

title: 110: Anime and Kaiju
description: The very definition of video entertainment from Japan.

title: 111: Artificial Intelligence
description: What makes machine intelligence “real AI”? And what is the difference between strong and weak AI?

title: 112: Donuts
description: We don’t know quite what an old-fashioned donut is, but we know what we like… and what we don’t.

title: 113: Art
description: I don’t know what it is, but I know it when I see it. John Siracusa and Jason Snell.

title: 114: Smoothie
description: If everything can be a smoothie, then nothing is. So we try to define what makes a smoothie and acts as a bulwark against the milkshake. John Siracusa and Jason Snell.

title: 115: Barbecue
description: Continuing our confused series of episodes about food-related topics, it’s time for John and Jason to talk about Jason’s favorite food style and what happens when you put food on a grill. John Siracusa and Jason Snell.

title: 116: Salad
description: From leafy greens to sugary Jell-O concoctions, all sorts of things are called salads. John Siracusa and Jason Snell.

title: 117: Brunch
description: We discuss the names of meals and when they happen, and make an interesting(?) digression into human sleep cycles. John Siracusa and Jason Snell.

title: 118: Ice Cream
description: It would seem like ice cream versus frozen yogurt would be the main debate. But the pronunciation of a third competitor completely derails us. John Siracusa and Jason Snell.

title: 119: Life
description: How can we call something alive? John Siracusa and Jason Snell.

title: 120: Death
description: Okay, time to call it. Time of death— wait, wait, everybody hold on. How do we define death? John Siracusa and Jason Snell.

title: 121: Holidays and Holiday Movies
description: What makes a movie a holiday movie? How do they celebrate winter holidays in warm climates? Merry Christmas to all, especially in Australia! John Siracusa and Jason Snell.

title: 122: Night (bark) Joggers (bark)
description: A dog interlude. John Siracusa and Jason Snell.

title: 123: Janet from "The Good Place"
description: Never believe what a robot tells you. John Siracusa and Jason Snell.

title: 124: The Trolley Problem
description: As recently highlighted on “The Good Place”, it’s a classic ethical conundum that John wants absolutely no part of. And what if the trolley drives itself? John Siracusa and Jason Snell.

title: 125: Cheesecake
description: Is cheesecake cheese, cake, pie, tart, or none of the above? Does the angle of the pan matter? Does crust content matter? Do any of us matter, really? John Siracusa and Jason Snell.

title: 126: Vacation
description: If you don’t go anywhere, is it a vacation? What if you go somewhere, but you don’t relax? John Siracusa and Jason Snell.

title: 127: Potato Chips
description: From Sour Cream & Onion to BBQ, what are the “real” potato chip flavors? John Siracusa and Jason Snell.

title: 128: The Midwest
description: Did both of Jason’s parents both come from the Midwest, or only one? What are the true boundaries of America’s heartland? John Siracusa and Jason Snell.

title: 129: Pets
description: What makes an animal a pet? John Siracusa and Jason Snell.

title: 130: Sweaters
description: Listener Ed, we’ve got bad news. John Siracusa and Jason Snell.

title: 131: Savory Donuts
description: Bagels are not donuts, people. John Siracusa and Jason Snell.

title: 132: Seasons
description: The conundrum of seasons versus eternally pleasant weather. John Siracusa and Jason Snell.

title: 133: Gnocchi
description: What makes pasta pasta? John Siracusa and Jason Snell.

title: 134: Personal Computers
description: Is a Mac a PC? Is an iPad a computer? Does John favor a broad definition or a narrow one? John Siracusa and Jason Snell.

title: 135: Reality TV
description: When is a game show a game show, and when is it reality television? Also, we reveal our favorite reality TV show. John Siracusa and Jason Snell.

title: 136: Programming
description: What is computer programming? And what doesn’t qualify? John Siracusa and Jason Snell.

title: 137: Nerds and Geeks
description: The subtle and vexing difference between a nerd and a geek. John Siracusa and Jason Snell.

title: 138: Job Security
description: John’s worked (and left) a lot of jobs. What’s his personal philosophy about job security versus going it alone as an independent? John Siracusa and Jason Snell.

title: 139: Planets, and also Pluto
description: John is given the opportunity to endorse or reject the rulings of the International Astronomical Union. John Siracusa and Jason Snell.

title: 140: Bread
description: Bread is bread, but what about hot dog buns, bagels, tortillas, and pitas? John Siracusa and Jason Snell.

title: 141: Podcasting
description: What makes something a podcast? OMG, are we one?! John Siracusa and Jason Snell.

title: 142: Toasters
description: Slot toasters, toaster ovens, and the definitions thereof. John Siracusa and Jason Snell.

title: 143: Phones
description: Smartphones, dumb phones, feature phones, and computers in your pocket. John Siracusa and Jason Snell.

title: 144: Soup
description: “You haven’t done soup yet, have you?” John Siracusa and Jason Snell.

title: 145: Database
description: Where spreadsheets and databases collide. John Siracusa and Jason Snell.

title: 146: GIF
description: Choosy mothers pronounce it differently. John Siracusa and Jason Snell.

title: 147: Cult
description: “Hokey religions and ancient weapons are no match for a good blaster at your side, kid.” Merry Christmas, everybody! John Siracusa and Jason Snell.

title: 148: Hacker
description: Do hackers do good, or bad, or both? John Siracusa and Jason Snell.

title: 149: Simulated Universe
description: Is this real or are we in a video game? How can we tell the true nature of the universe? John Siracusa and Jason Snell.

title: 150: Marty the Supermarket Robot
description: In a rare topical episode, John and Jason discuss Marty, the tall, googly-eyed robot that may soon be roaming the aisles of a supermarket near you. Does Marty meet the Roomba test? Are the googly eyes fooling anyone? John Siracusa and Jason Snell.

title: 151: "Chick Flick"
description: What is a “Chick Flick”? Let’s start off by taking apart the term itself. John Siracusa and Jason Snell.

title: 152: Milk
description: Legal news: Is Almond Milk milk? John Siracusa and Jason Snell.

title: 153: Live Action
description: If the new “Lion King” film features CGI animals talking with other CGI animals, is it a “live-action” movie or just a different kind of animation? What about a movie like “Avengers: Infinity War”? John Siracusa and Jason Snell.

title: 154: American Food
description: It all goes back to Mesopotamia. John Siracusa and Jason Snell.

title: 155: TV and Movies
description: When is it a TV show and when is it a movie? It’s confusing. John Siracusa and Jason Snell.

title: 156: Combination Restaurants
description: We’ll see you at the Carl’s Jr./Green Burrito/KFC/Taco Bell. John Siracusa and Jason Snell.

title: 157: Board Games
description: How much board is required? John Siracusa and Jason Snell.

title: 158: Pants
description: The entire conversation is pants. (The Brits will get that.) John Siracusa and Jason Snell.

title: 159: Campus Delivery Robots
description: Prompted by a note from Listener Zach, we discuss the trend of “autonomous food delivery vehicles” on college campuses. John Siracusa and Jason Snell.

title: 160: Bacon
description: By popular demand, John has done his research—or maybe not?—and is here to break down what is bacon and what is an impostor. John Siracusa and Jason Snell.

title: 161: Storefronts
description: Select all the STOREFRONTS to prove that you’re a human. John Siracusa and Jason Snell.

title: 162: Doors
description: What about when they’re ajar? John Siracusa and Jason Snell.

title: 163: Family
description: What constitutes family? Blood relatives only? Are friends family? Are co-workers family? Can you escape your family? John Siracusa and Jason Snell.

title: 164: Cover Version
description: Listener Luke sent in this week’s theme song. Is it a cover version of our canonical theme song? When is a new version of a song not a cover? John Siracusa and Jason Snell.

title: 165: Leftovers
description: When does a meal turn into leftovers? John Siracusa and Jason Snell.

title: 166: Smart Devices
description: Where do we draw the line between a regular device and a “smart” device? John Siracusa and Jason Snell.

title: 167: Pet Names
description: Can we differentiate between how people name pets and how they name children? Listeners Rover and Whiskers, drop us a line. John Siracusa and Jason Snell.

title: 168: Augmented Reality
description: An Accidental AR podcast. John Siracusa and Jason Snell.

title: 169: Burgers
description: And do sliders have to slide? John Siracusa and Jason Snell.

title: 170: City
description: Does it all come down to the U.S. Postal Service? John Siracusa and Jason Snell.

title: 171: Dish
description: From dish to plate to bowl. John Siracusa and Jason Snell.

title: 172: Soup, Part II
description: Is soup a drink? What separates liquids from food? John Siracusa and Jason Snell.

title: 173: River
description: When is a body of water a river? John Siracusa and Jason Snell.

title: 174: Reading
description: It’s fundamental, yes. But is it something you can do with your ears? John Siracusa and Jason Snell.

title: 175: Beard
description: When is it stubble and when is it more? John Siracusa and Jason Snell.

title: 176: Swipe Right
description: Where does your finger go when you “swipe right”? John Siracusa and Jason Snell.

title: 177: Walking Distance
description: It’s within walking distance. How far is that? John Siracusa and Jason Snell.

title: 178: Morning
description: Morning has broken, like the first… morning? John Siracusa and Jason Snell.

title: 179: Grocery Store
description: But what if they also sell shampoo there? John Siracusa and Jason Snell.

title: 180: Tabs
description: Tabs or spaces? AFTERSHOW: Commas. John Siracusa and Jason Snell.

title: 181: Camera
description: My other car is also a camera. John Siracusa and Jason Snell.

title: 182: Working From Home
description: Whatever this is called, a lot of us are doing it these days. John Siracusa and Jason Snell.

title: 183: Slots and Ports
description: Is a port a slot? PCMCIA cards have slots, but USB devices have ports. Either way, Jason has to make amends. John Siracusa and Jason Snell.

title: 184: Indie Developer
description: What’s an Indie Developer, and is John one now? What does it mean to be “indie?” John Siracusa and Jason Snell.

title: 185: Blanket
description: Listener James sends us a special message from beneath his blanket. John Siracusa and Jason Snell.

title: 186: Gum
description: Most people aren’t eating light bulbs. John Siracusa and Jason Snell.

title: 187: The Cloud
description: Is The Cloud just Other People’s Computers? Watch out for Cloud Men! John Siracusa and Jason Snell.

title: 188: Reboot
description: Beginning in this episode, Chris Pine and Zachary Quinto will be portraying John and Jason. Or not. John Siracusa and Jason Snell.

title: 189: What We're Owed
description: When a book series hasn’t completed, what does the author owe us? John Siracusa and Jason Snell.

title: 190: Pillow
description: You can use this podcast as a pillow, if you like, but it’s still not a pillow. John Siracusa and Jason Snell.

title: 191: Game
description: The universe is Candy Land. John Siracusa and Jason Snell.

title: 192: Backup Brain
description: If we clone your body and transfer your memories to it, is it you? John Siracusa and Jason Snell.

title: 193: Puppet
description: When is it a puppet, and when is it just someone in a suit? And what does this mean for the future of Gritty? John Siracusa and Jason Snell.

title: 194: Henge
description: When the definition escapes its antecedent. John Siracusa and Jason Snell.

title: 195: Child
description: When is a child no longer a child? John Siracusa and Jason Snell.

title: 196: Video
description: Is a GIF a video? (Incomparable members also get a bonus episode about movie studio logos, released today.) John Siracusa and Jason Snell.

title: 197: Indoors
description: When are we indoors and when are we outdoors? And where do tents fit in? John Siracusa and Jason Snell.

title: 198: Soda
description: Fizzy water. Is it soda, or pop, or a soft drink, or something else? (Incomparable members also get a bonus episode about Coca-Cola and cocaine, also released today.) John Siracusa and Jason Snell.

title: 199: Christmas Special
description: In the spirit of the season, we discuss when a Christmas tree is dead. (Thanks to Listener Darran.) John Siracusa and Jason Snell.

title: 200: Microscopic "Robots"
description: We celebrate our 200th episode by going back to where it all started—news about whether something is a robot or not. Also, we may have inadvertently started a religion. (Congratulations, Listener Eric!) John Siracusa and Jason Snell.

title: 201: Apocalypse
description: On the occasion of the 100th anniversary of the robot, happy stuff: When does the apocalypse start, and when do we reach post-apocalyptic times? John Siracusa and Jason Snell.

title: 202: Books
description: Is a book a bound, printed collection of pages, or is it something more? John Siracusa and Jason Snell.

title: 203: Bagel Update
description: A very unfortunate bagel on either side of the Atlantic. John Siracusa and Jason Snell.

title: 204: Peanut Butter
description: Chances are pretty good that the peanut butter you eat is terrible. John Siracusa and Jason Snell.

title: 205: Pots and Pans
description: What divides pots from pans? John Siracusa and Jason Snell.

title: 206: Relish
description: Not all pickles are pickles, and not all relish is pickle relish. John Siracusa and Jason Snell.

title: 207: Pandemic Changes (or not)
description: Has the pandemic made John reconsider some of his previous rulings? (One guess.) John Siracusa and Jason Snell.

title: 208: Self-Driving Cars, Part 2
description: Tim Cook thinks that self-driving cars are robots. Does John want to revisit his opinion? John Siracusa and Jason Snell.

title: 209: Dog-Shaped Dogs
description: What is the shape of a dog? John Siracusa and Jason Snell.

title: 210: Burrito, Part 2 (Qdoba v. Panera)
description: The strange case of the burrito sandwich. John Siracusa and Jason Snell.

title: 211: Rules for Watching TV
description: Do you always start watching at the beginning? And do you have to watch till the end? John Siracusa and Jason Snell.

title: 212: Dishwasher
description: When do you run the dishwasher? Do you rinse the dishes first? And wouldn’t it be nice if our dishwashers were robots? John Siracusa and Jason Snell.

title: 213: Daylight Saving Time
description: Should we really spring forward and fall back? John Siracusa and Jason Snell.

title: 214: Religious or Spiritual
description: When you see an org chart and money changes hands, your spirituality has become something else. John Siracusa and Jason Snell.

title: 215: A Criterion of Data
description: Singular or plural? John Siracusa and Jason Snell.

title: 216: Grocery Robot Swarm
description: If robots at a grocery-store warehouse works in tandem, are they robots? If they have a hive mind, are they still robots? John Siracusa and Jason Snell.

title: 217: Floating Bridge
description: Listener Isaac wants us to judge if a certain “floating bridge” is actually a ferry. This leads, of course, to a discussion of infinite bridges and whether a fairy is a ferry in California. John Siracusa and Jason Snell.

title: 218: Photo
description: Listener Beth seeks enlightenment about what makes something a photo. John Siracusa and Jason Snell.

title: 219: Camping
description: Listeners Jono and Chris, and friend Tony Sindelar, have questions about what John defines as ‘camping.’ Suffering is surprisingly part of the calculation. John Siracusa and Jason Snell.

title: 220: Popcorn
description: The proper way to eat popcorn. ðŸ¿ John Siracusa and Jason Snell.

title: 221: Cooking
description: What’s cooking? Is making tea cooking? John’s answers may surprise you. They certainly surprised Jason. John Siracusa and Jason Snell.

title: 222: Sundays
description: Do Sundays start the week, or end it? When does the week end, and is that the weekend? John Siracusa and Jason Snell.

title: 223: Money
description: What makes something money? Is gold money? Is Bitcoin? John Siracusa and Jason Snell.

title: 224: Next Wednesday
description: When is Next Wednesday? Is it Wednesday? Or the Wednesday after that? John Siracusa and Jason Snell.

title: 225: Car
description: What makes a car a car, and not a truck, or an SUV, or a crossover? John Siracusa and Jason Snell.

title: 226: Email, and Preparing the Way (for Roombas)
description: Jason starts to ask John a question, but everything gets derailed. John Siracusa and Jason Snell.

title: 227: Semi-Homemade Cooking with John Siracusa
description: Listener Scott wants to know what “homemade” cooking is. Jason made this episode from scratch. (But the theme song was store-bought.) John Siracusa and Jason Snell.

title: 228: America
description: Why do Americans crowd out the rest of two continents from the namespace? John thinks it’s about imperialism; Jason thinks it’s because our country has no proper name. John Siracusa and Jason Snell.

title: 229: Friendship
description: Listener Ashley wants to know about the true meaning of friendship. John Siracusa and Jason Snell.

title: 230: Accents
description: John has one, but also doesn’t have one. Mary married some merry carrots. John Siracusa and Jason Snell.

title: 231: CAPTCHAs of South African "robots"
description: Select all ROBOT RELATED PODCASTS. If there are none, click Stop. John Siracusa and Jason Snell.

title: 232: Stillsuits
description: Paul Atreides and the Fremen sure look cool, but won’t they die of hyperthermia in those suits? (Incomparable Members will find a special bonus episode of Robot or Not in the First Class feed today. Become a member for lots of goodies!) John Siracusa and Jason Snell.

title: 233: Magnetic Slime
description: Does texture matter when it comes to robots? John Siracusa and Jason Snell.

title: 234: Pasta Draft
description: A bunch of baseball writers drafted pastas. John has thoughts. John Siracusa and Jason Snell.

title: 235: Robot Loathing
description: Listener/Professor Lisa can handle conceptual analysis on her own, but she does wonder why campus delivery robots make her so angry. (It wasn’t just because they’re Russian.) John Siracusa and Jason Snell.

title: 236: Stay-at-Home Moms
description: We salute all Moms, no matter their classification. John Siracusa and Jason Snell.

title: 237: Cameos
description: Is that just a really short acting part, or is it only a cameo? John Siracusa and Jason Snell.

title: 238: Electronic vs. Electric
description: When is something electronic, and when is it electric? John Siracusa and Jason Snell.

title: 239: Monolith
description: It’s a big thing in the middle of nowhere. Does it need to be a rock to be a monolith? John Siracusa and Jason Snell.

title: 240: Holes in a Straw
description: Topology can be tricky. John Siracusa and Jason Snell.

title: 241: Voltron
description: Many robots, one robot, or no robots? John Siracusa and Jason Snell.

title: 242: A Group of Robots
description: When robots flock together naturally, will humans give them a name? Or will we be too busy dying? John Siracusa and Jason Snell.

title: 243: Wheels and Doors
description: Sometimes, everyone on the Internet wants John’s opinion. John Siracusa and Jason Snell.

title: 244: House or Boat?
description: It’s a house, but it floats. John Siracusa and Jason Snell.

title: 245: Werewolves
description: If you’re a werewolf, are you a werewolf all the time? John Siracusa and Jason Snell.

title: 246: Undead Zombie Spider Robots
description: Spooky! John Siracusa and Jason Snell.

title: 247: Garlic
description: Is garlic a vegetable, an herb, a spice, or what? John Siracusa and Jason Snell.

title: 248: The Follow-Up Episode
description: For the very first time, we do some housekeeping about holes, Russian robots, salad, genocide, Voltron, and available sales leads. John Siracusa and Jason Snell.

title: 249: Blaine the Mono
description: Blaine is a pain, and that is the truth. John Siracusa and Jason Snell.

title: 250: Roomba Update
description: Some deeper questions about whether certain Roomba behavior makes it more or less of a robot. John Siracusa and Jason Snell.

title: 251: Happy New Year
description: Are we too late to say it? John Siracusa and Jason Snell.

title: 252: Friend of the Show
description: Listener Rob and Listener Reiner, who are not Director Rob Reiner, want to know if they are Friends of the Show. John Siracusa and Jason Snell.

title: 253: University
description: What makes a university? Is it the buildings, or the people, or the big hole you throw money into? John Siracusa and Jason Snell.

title: 254: Shoes
description: Shoes, socks, sandals, boots. Footwear is complicated. John Siracusa and Jason Snell.

title: 255: Ice
description: Listener Chris clues us into an important ice safety campaign. John Siracusa and Jason Snell.

title: 256: Stepmom
description: Sometimes they’re wicked, sometimes not. Can an adult call a parent’s new wife a stepmom? Bonus: Can you be too old to be an orphan? John Siracusa and Jason Snell.

title: 257: Island
description: The difference between islands and continents, and also why Pluto can be a planet if you want to lower your standards. John Siracusa and Jason Snell.

title: 258: Beach
description: Where do beaches exist? And what materials do they need to be comprised of? John Siracusa and Jason Snell.

title: 259: Ports
description: Don’t anthromorphize ports. They hate that. John Siracusa and Jason Snell.

title: 260: Dish v. Plate (revisited)
description: Jason’s trip to his mother’s house makes him rethink his definition of what a dish is. Also, he gets some upsetting news about the long-term relationship between the fork and the spoon. John Siracusa and Jason Snell.

title: 261: Buildings
description: A chair is not a house and house is not a home, but is a house a building? And what about gazebos? John Siracusa and Jason Snell.

title: 262: Keys
description: If any device can open a door, is every device a key? John Siracusa and Jason Snell.

title: 263: Shade
description: This time we’re throwing shade. But do sunglasses? John Siracusa and Jason Snell.

title: 264: Cookie Dough
description: If it’s never meant to make a cookie, is it still cookie dough? (Also: Peanut Butter Spread, Cheese Food, and other food labeling we have known.) John Siracusa and Jason Snell.

title: 265: Frown
description: ☹️ John Siracusa and Jason Snell.

title: 266: AI Camerabot
description: Finally we talk about robots again. If a robot controls a camera, is it a camera robot? John Siracusa and Jason Snell.

title: 267: Hiatus
description: Listener Magnus is concerned that his favorite podcast is on hiatus. When is something on hiatus and when is it cancelled? John Siracusa and Jason Snell.

title: 268: Sigh
description: Listener Jamie wonders whether his dog is really sighing. We discuss noises dogs make. Also, after posting our previous episode we realized we got the numbering of the podcast out of order. Sigh. John Siracusa and Jason Snell.

title: 269: The Worst
description: Listener Andrew is worried that things we say are “the worst” are really just bad. John Siracusa and Jason Snell.

title: 270: Relay FM Podcastathon Special
description: Live from the Relay FM Podcastathon, Jason and special guest Stephen Hackett ask John a bunch of questions from the Robot Or Not question list. Topics include: Toast, Roadkill, Sandwich Order of Operations, Garage, and Cereal Soup. Please donate to St. Jude and help move us one step closer to the day where no child dies from cancer. John Siracusa and Jason Snell with Stephen Hackett.

title: 271: Nachos
description: Hold on, John, Jason’s got this one. John Siracusa and Jason Snell.

title: 272: Spoiler Policy
description: Listener Nick wonders what John’s policy on spoilers is. (Spoilers for “Romeo and Juliet” and “Citizen Kane.”) John Siracusa and Jason Snell.

title: 273: Lies
description: On John’s other podcast, Casey Liss often says he lied when he means he made a mistake. So what is a lie? (Trust us, we totally answer this one.) John Siracusa and Jason Snell.

title: 274: Avoid All Robots
description: Some timely news regarding a university warning its community members to “avoid all robots.” John Siracusa and Jason Snell.

title: 275: Musician
description: When is someone a musician? Are DJs musicians? And more importantly, are John and Jason musicians? John Siracusa and Jason Snell.

title: 276: Italian Ice
description: A perfectly normal discussion of Italian Ice takes a left turn and goes into outer space, where other ices are available. John Siracusa and Jason Snell.

title: 277: Coffee
description: A question about cold brew coffee makes us question everything about coffee. Is everything coffee? Probably not. John Siracusa and Jason Snell.

title: 278: Spatula
description: Spatulas, scrapers, flippers, and home economics. John Siracusa and Jason Snell.

title: 279: Streets
description: I want to run, I want to hide, I want to tear down the walls that hold me inside. Sometimes the streets have no name, but other times they are named roads, or avenues, or boulevards, or drives. What does it all mean? Does Jason live on a road or a drive? When we go there, we go there with you. It’s all we can do. John Siracusa and Jason Snell.

title: 280: Hat
description: What makes a hat a hat? John Siracusa and Jason Snell.

title: 281: Killer Robot
description: Listener Kent is building actual killer robots. John Siracusa and Jason Snell.

title: 282: Places You've Been
description: Do you have to leave the airport or get out of the car to claim you’ve been somewhere? (And are you under oath?) John Siracusa and Jason Snell.

title: 283: (Pizza) Pie
description: Fresh out of the oven for Pi Day, here’s a discussion of who exactly thinks pizza is a pie. John Siracusa and Jason Snell.

title: 284: ⚾️ Robot Umps ⚾️
description: It’s baseball’s Opening Day, so here’s our discussion of automated balls and strikes, also known as “Robot Umps,” how they relate to automated Hawk-Eye tennis calls, and why we won’t ever know how good human umpires could actually be. John Siracusa and Jason Snell.

title: 285: Theme Songs / Skip Intro
description: We follow up on some feedback about our theme songs, and theme songs in general, while taking on whether we use the Skip Intro button when we should be listening to TV theme songs. John Siracusa and Jason Snell.

title: 286: Dishwashing Methods
description: A tale of dishwashers and large sinks. John Siracusa and Jason Snell.

title: 287: Autonomous Excavator
description: Listener Ivan sent in a link to an autonomous excavator that assembled a six-foot wall out of rocks. Is it the Roomba of construction materials?! John Siracusa and Jason Snell.

title: 288: El Camino
description: Thanks to Friend of the Show Casey, we’re talking about weird cars and car classes again. John Siracusa and Jason Snell.

title: 289: Vending Machine
description: Friend of the show Frank is seeking to delineate when something is a “vending machine” and when it’s just a machine that vends. John Siracusa and Jason Snell.

title: 290: Airport Wheelchair
description: Listener Erik sent us this video of self-navigating wheelchairs in the Miami Airport. Does the Roomba Rule apply? John Siracusa and Jason Snell.

title: 291: Hawaiian Shirts
description: Are Hawaiian shirts just fun to wear, or are they cultural appropriation? John Siracusa and Jason Snell.

title: 292: Tea
description: Is “truffle mushroom tea” just a soup? Did a fancy New York restaurant play a trick on Listener David and his wife? And what is tea, really? John Siracusa and Jason Snell.

title: 293: Severe Weather
description: Listener Arne received a severe weather alert for a fire. Fires are very bad, but are they weather? Are some natural disasters weather, and others not? John Siracusa and Jason Snell.

title: 294: Double Space
description: Listener Daniel would like John’s blessing for his practice of putting two spaces after every sentence he types. John Siracusa and Jason Snell.

title: 295: Homepods and Other Robots (or Not)
description: In a rare timely episode, John and Jason discuss a report from Bloomberg’s Mark Gurman that Apple is designing a series of robots, including a “robot” that sits on a table and moves its display around, and a “robot” that follows you around your house folding laundry, reminding you of your mortality, and possibly running a viral campaign for Apple TV+ shows. John Siracusa and Jason Snell.

title: 296: Catchphrase
description: Oh, Listener Sean wants to know about catchphrases! Well, isn’t that special? John Siracusa and Jason Snell.

title: 297: Relay Podcastathon Special 2024
description: Live from the Relay Podcastathon, Jason and special guest Casey Liss ask John a bunch of questions from the Robot Or Not question list. Topics include: All-In-One computers, dates, pasta, and antique vs. retro. It’s Childhood Cancer Awareness Month. Please consider donating as a part of our campaign at stjude.org/relay. John Siracusa and Jason Snell with Casey Liss.
exclusion_reason: Live Relay Podcastathon special: a grab-bag of questions from the list (all-in-one computers, dates, pasta, antique vs. retro) with no single topic the ruling rests on.

title: 298: Henchman
description: As so often happens with us, discussions of evil henchman end up becoming discussions of legal employment status. John Siracusa and Jason Snell.

title: 299: Window
description: I can see clearly now. John Siracusa and Jason Snell.

title: 300: Fast Food
description: There are so many different ways to define fast food. Is pizza fast food? Also, Jason has a story about the Shake Shake in the Minneapolis airport. John Siracusa and Jason Snell.

title: 301: Fan/Light
description: Listener Patrick is concerned about taxonomy, most particularly involving fans that are also lights. John Siracusa and Jason Snell.

title: 302: Sandwich Legal Update
description: Many listeners are concerned about recent legal rulings that suggest tacos and burritos are sandwiches. But we all know who the real voice of authority is. John Siracusa and Jason Snell.

title: 303: Tipping
description: Listener Ben and his sister-in-law have come up with a sophisticated system of rules for when and when not to leave a gratuity. But someone else may have his own rules. John Siracusa and Jason Snell.

title: 304: Calendar Year
description: Listener Alexander has seen through the calendar’s deceptions and wants to know why any old day couldn’t be the start of a new year. When does the year begin in our hearts? (Happy New Year, everyone!) John Siracusa and Jason Snell.

title: 305: Console
description: Is a Game Boy a game console? What about a Switch? Can a handheld gaming device also be a console? What makes something a console? John Siracusa and Jason Snell.

title: 306: Roomba-like Items
description: In the end, the Grain Weevils and robot lawn mowers come for us all. John Siracusa and Jason Snell.

title: 307: Sandwich Legal Update II
description: Two listeners have requested that we revisit recent court and podcast rulings regarding the definition of a sandwich. Also, Jason details his meager high-school lunch. John Siracusa and Jason Snell.

title: 308: Gibson Robot Guitar
description: Listener Jason (not that one) wants to know if the Gibson Robot Guitar is just trying to jump on the robot bandwagon as a form of fancy marketing. John Siracusa and Jason Snell.

title: 309: Flying
description: Listeners Joshua and Matthias want to know about flying in (or on) an airplane. John Siracusa and Jason Snell.

title: 310: Arc
description: Listener Victor brings us a question from another “or Not?” podcast about how many points are required to make something a story, episode, or character arc. John Siracusa and Jason Snell.

title: 311: Mushroombot
description: Listener Jim wants John to weigh in on the story of the mushroom that was given a robot body, and while that does sound fascinating, the answer seems to be right there in the description. John Siracusa and Jason Snell.

title: 312: Unanchored Buoys
description: Listener Ben asks: If a Buoy is unanchored and works hard to stay where it is, is it the Roomba of the seas? John Siracusa and Jason Snell.

title: 313: Tech
description: Listener Jason (not host Jason) wants to know if “non-tech items” are really tech items. John Siracusa and Jason Snell.

title: 314: Bay Leaf
description: Listener Paul doubts the efficacy of the Bay Leaf. Host John ponders the longevity of Spices. Host Jason admits to keeping spices 15 years past their expiration dates. John Siracusa and Jason Snell.

title: 315: 10th Anniversary Episode
description: Let’s get back to basics. We celebrate our improbable 10th anniversary with a letter from Listener Scott, who has a lot of questions about his son’s book “Science Comics: Robots and Drones.” John Siracusa and Jason Snell.

title: 316: Spacesuits
description: Listener Lorne asks what makes a spacesuit a spacesuit, and it gets complicated in a hurry. John Siracusa and Jason Snell.

title: 317: AI Hype
description: Listener Christian, your time has come. Is an AI Lock the same as a Smart Lock? Or a Fuzzy Logic Lock? When bicycle gear shifters are called “AI”, how do we define what any of this means? I know—let’s ask John. John Siracusa and Jason Snell.

title: 318: Charger
description: Listener Eric really needs his kids to differentiate between charger blocks and charging cables. John Siracusa and Jason Snell.

title: 319: Market
description: Listener Marc ponders the “VR headset market” and wants to know what makes a market a market. John Siracusa and Jason Snell.

title: 320: Parasol
description: Summer is in full swing, so Listener Ken has asked us to differentiate between umbrellas and parasols. John Siracusa and Jason Snell.

title: 321: Glass
description: Can a drinking glass be made out of plastic? Or is it just a cup? John Siracusa and Jason Snell.

title: 322: Vehicle
description: Listener Eric asks if vehicles are only motorized, and we ponder how small a thing can be before it’s not a vehicle anymore. John Siracusa and Jason Snell.

title: 323: Pasta Roundup
description: John fields some important questions about pasta from listeners Connor, Joshua, and Lee, including the definition of Al Dente and noodles versus pasta. John Siracusa and Jason Snell.

title: 324: Landscaper
description: Who scapes the lands? Who gardens the gardens? Who mows and who blows? Not us! John Siracusa and Jason Snell.

title: 325: Wire
description: Listener Matt can’t stand it when someone calls a USB cable a wire. But what does John think? John Siracusa and Jason Snell.

title: 326: Spiders and Other Bugs
description: Listener Kev needs us to unpack John’s comment about “spiders and other bugs.” Does that mean spiders are bugs? And what are the other bugs? Spooky! John Siracusa and Jason Snell.

title: 327: Blogs
description: What’s a blog, and what’s a news outlet? Are Jason and John bloggers? John Siracusa and Jason Snell.

title: 328: Hoodie
description: Stephen Hackett has called us out and requests John’s ruling. John Siracusa and Jason Snell.

title: 329: Charger follow-up
description: Listener William challenges our ruling about chargers and we get deep into the weeds of car charging. John Siracusa and Jason Snell.

title: 330: Sleigh
description: The difference between a slegh and a sled. John Siracusa and Jason Snell.

title: 331: Supercars and Hypercars
description: Host John Siracusa asks himself to discuss the difference between Supercars and Hypercars, while Jason looks on. John Siracusa and Jason Snell.

title: 332: Basement
description: Listener Joel has discovered some Canadians referring to the first floor of a two-story house as a “basement.” Does this defy all reason? How low must you go to be a basement? John Siracusa and Jason Snell.

title: 333: Scrolling
description: Listener Scott’s wife sure has a strange definition of which way is up. John Siracusa and Jason Snell.

title: 334: Open-Faced Sandwiches and French Bread Pizzas
description: Listener Gregory tries to confuse us with a question about open-faced sandwiches and pizza. We largely ignore him and talk about different ways to eat things that are like pizza, but aren’t quite pizza. John Siracusa and Jason Snell.

title: 335: Pop-Tart Pie
description: Listener Gregory thinks Pop-Tarts are pies. We have ratio questions. Also: We remember so many burned palates caused by calzones and McDonald’s fruit pies. John Siracusa and Jason Snell.

title: 336: Building
description: Listener Jack wants to know if a few famous gates and statues are also buildings. John Siracusa and Jason Snell.

title: 337: Shirt
description: Listener Roy brings us into his debate with his teenage son about what makes a shirt a shirt. John Siracusa and Jason Snell.

title: 338: Facial Hair
description: Listener Justin tries to get us to stretch the definition of “facial hair” beyond the beard. John Siracusa and Jason Snell.

title: 339: Can
description: Listener Niels follows on from the logical question of if a glass can be made of plastic to ponder what makes a can a can. John Siracusa and Jason Snell.

title: 340: Out of Pocket
description: Listener Tom really wants us to explain what it means if someone is “out of pocket.” This leads to some existential questions about the pocket and the people who may not be in it. John Siracusa and Jason Snell.

title: 341: Life on the Moon (and Mars?)
description: Listener Jack seeks a true definition of what it means when we say “humans will live on the Moon (or Mars).” Does a brief visit count? Do you need to grow your own potatoes? John Siracusa and Jason Snell.

title: 342: Superhero Naming Conventions
description: Listener Joshua is really focused on the grammar of Superhero and Supervillain names. Is Batman a bat? Does Doctor Doom have an advanced degree? Can Rogue keep her name while joining the X-Men? Are there any rules at all? John Siracusa and Jason Snell.

title: 343: Pizza Robot
description: Live from Estes Park, Colorado, listener Kyle has eaten at a pizza place where his food was delivered via a robot! But… is it a robot, or not? After a swift verdict, John and Jason then spend far more time digging deep on Antonio’s Pizza and what sort of pizza it provides to the people of Colorado. John Siracusa and Jason Snell.

title: 344: Look-Up
description: Listener Jason used ChatGPT to find information that answered a colleague’s question. But did he “look it up?” John Siracusa and Jason Snell.

title: 345: Wearable Robot
description: Listener Caleb saw an ergonomics assistance backpack at a trade show, advertised as a robot. Can you wear… a robot? John Siracusa and Jason Snell.

title: 346: Pizza Wheel
description: Listener Ed doesn’t keep his pizza wheel in his knife, but it’s got a blade and cuts things. What makes a knife a knife? John Siracusa and Jason Snell.

title: 347: Official
description: Unofficial Fan of “Robot or Not” Alexander wants to know what makes something official. Why are David Smith’s transcripts of The Talk Show “unofficial” if John Gruber links to them? John Siracusa and Jason Snell.

title: 348: Colloquial Robot
description: Listener Matt has caught John in a trap, because once on ATP John referred to something as a robot that is not a robot. Does John use his own definitions in real life? Are podcasts real life? What is the meaning of this?! John Siracusa and Jason Snell.

title: 349: Video Game
description: Listeners Mark and Matt wants to know if everything on a screen is a video game. Jason ponders the idea that a PDF printout of a crossword puzzle could be a video game. John says that he is being silly and he should take these questions more seriously. John Siracusa and Jason Snell.

title: 350: Pasta Sauce
description: Listener Griffin wonders what you could put on pasta that would arguably make it a sauce. John probably considers this sacrilege, but here we are. John Siracusa and Jason Snell.

title: 351: Cobot
description: Listener Paul has heard the term “cobot” to refer to “collaborative robots,” but can a robot that requires a human to function really be a robot? John Siracusa and Jason Snell.

title: 352: 'Wolf-Inspired' Robot
description: Listener Santiago wonders if a ‘wolf-inspired’ vehicle from Kawasaki is a robot, a metal horse, or just a vehicle. John Siracusa and Jason Snell.

title: 353: Stuffing/Dressing
description: Listener Wes has a Scotland-based observation about whether baked potatoes are stuffed or dressed. Seems straightforward, innit? John Siracusa and Jason Snell.

title: 354: Tennis Robot (Derogatory)
description: Just in time for Wimbledon, Listener Muhammad provides a “tennis robot” for us to judge. We issue a judgment, but we’re not particularly happy about it. John Siracusa and Jason Snell.

title: 355: Hikes and Walks
description: Listener Tim asks us about when a walk becomes a hike. Is it about topology? Degree of difficulty? Those seeking hard and fast rules may be frustrated by the result. John Siracusa and Jason Snell.

title: 356: Card Game
description: Listener Steven makes a lot of assumptions about what games are card games, but we set him straight. John Siracusa and Jason Snell.

title: 357: More Boats
description: Listener Joseph is unclear about where rafts fit into the whole boat hierarchy. We also toss some kayaks, canoes, and submarines into the water. John Siracusa and Jason Snell.

title: 358: (Parenthetical) Song Titles
description: If you can’t hear part of this episode it’s because that part was in parentheses. Thanks to (Listener) Charlie for sending in this question. John Siracusa and Jason Snell.

title: 359: Overseas
description: Is a place overseas if you don’t have to go over a sea to get there? John Siracusa and Jason Snell.

title: 360: Douglas Adams
description: The Encyclopedia Galactica defines a robot as a mechanical apparatus designed to do the work of a man. The marketing division of the Sirius Cybernetics Corporation defines a robot as “Your Plastic Pal Who’s Fun to Be With.” The Hitchhiker’s Guide to the Galaxy defines the marketing division of the Sirius Cybernetic Corporation as “a bunch of mindless jerks who’ll be the first against the wall when the revolution comes.” John Siracusa and Jason Snell.

title: 361: Car Wash
description: Is a car wash a building with machinery in it or a robot? This question allows us to flip the “episodes since ‘Robot or Not’ was about robots” sign back to zero. John Siracusa and Jason Snell.

title: 362: Robot? Pas robot?
description: Curiosity, c’est un robot! Robot de cuisine, ce n’est pas un robot! Thanks to Listener Erik and the Cité des Sciences et de l’Industrie. John Siracusa and Jason Snell.

title: 62b: Filesystems and Flowerpot Robots
description: Live from RelayCon WWDC 2016, it’s a special live edition of Robot or Not.
